mathematical_checks: The sign-class embedding PSL2R into symmetric matrices vv^t is proper and injective. Its one-point compactification is compact metric. Uniform convergence of distance-to-closed-set functions yields a genuine Hausdorff closed-set limit; finite points give subgroup closure under products/inverses.

The uniform base displacement bound passes to every nonidentity finite limit. It supplies a uniform identity gap, discreteness and eventual equality of simultaneous approximants to one element. Every fixed finite relation is therefore eventually exact, without assuming finite presentation.

Squared trace at least4 passes to limits; nonidentity elliptics and torsion are excluded. The quotient model applies also to infinitely generated and infinite-area groups. The invariant H2 quotient embeds isometrically as a closed subspace of the H3 quotient by equality of orbit-distance infima.

Small quotient discs inject on a neighborhood of their closures for late n: any contrary deck identifications have bounded displacement, hence a convergent matrix subsequence, contradicting limit injectivity and the uniform identity gap. Compact overlaps have only finitely many possible deck transforms by the same properness argument.

Exact finite cocycles and convergent chart transitions are obtained by eventual finite relations. Disjoint source compact subdiscs remain disjoint, yielding actual asymptotic separation, not just coefficient convergence.

In the Lorentz blend, sigma_a=g_ab sigma_b and g_ac=g_ab g_bc. The base-b sum uses g_ab,n inverse; on changing to c the entire sum transforms by g_bc,n inverse. Future timelike positivity permits normalization, so the maps glue exactly and converge smoothly to identity. No holomorphicity of these compact-region maps is claimed.

Compact injectivity of the blended maps follows first from separation for distinct limiting points and then from a local derivative lower bound near a common limiting point. Thus actual compact-region embeddings follow. Cover extraction for arbitrary subgroups uses the same identity gap; local common charts give convergent covering maps without a normality or finite-degree premise.

The Dirichlet domain has locally finite bisectors: one meeting radiusR forces base displacement at most2R. Its boundary is a countable union of null geodesics. The finite-type area calculation uses supplied cusp charts. At y=T the outward normal is +e2, boundary tangent -e1, and inward normal -e2, giving geodesic curvature -1. Boundary lengths and omitted cusp areas both equal ell/T; Gauss-Bonnet therefore gives total area2pi(2g-2+N), including the closed case.
